title: Ranking All 20 Premier League Teams’ Performances on Matchday 8
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom6:00 PM EDTThere was a real contrast of emotions across the Premier League weekend. / Dan Istitene/Getty Images (Dalot), Liverpool FC/Getty Images (Isak), Julian Finney/Getty Images (Gabriel)The Real Madrid legend Alfredo Di Stéfano used to say: “A game without a goal is like a day without sunshine.” There was no sun spotted on English shores as Storm Boelo washed across the nation, coating every match in a wall of rain powered by an unrelenting wind. But, fortunately for those of a Di Stéfano persuasion, there was only one 0–0 draw.
Some managed to tiptoe between the raindrops while others were caught in the deluge on a Premier League weekend which could have lasting ramifications.

The illusions of a pre-appeal title race took a twist on Saturday before Manchester United sunk to a new nadir 24 hours later. Liverpool’s signings actually started clicking and Tottenham Hotspur even managed to win a game at Stamford Bridge.

It didn’t go Mason Mount’s way. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesWhile Michael Carrick’s precarious future could understandably distract from the machinations on the pitch, it should not be overlooked how dreadful Manchester United were, once again.Any whisper of threat which the hosts were able to muster came long after the result had been decided, with United—shorn of their divisive creative lynchpin Bruno Fernandes—resolutely devoid of any attacking spark. Bournemouth, by contrast, could afford to miss half of the Opta-defined “big chances” they created and still romp to a comfortable 3–0 win.

Xabi Alonso oversaw Chelsea’s first home defeat to Tottenham since 2018. / Glyn KIRK/AFP/Getty ImagesThis was not a high spec contest of quality action. At times, it was reminiscent of two bald men fighting over a comb. Neither team had much use for the ball, which scarcely looked like finding the back of the net until Chelsea’s stand-in goalkeeper Mike Penders handed Tottenham the lead. Cole Palmer capped off a night of infamy with two entirely needless yellow cards.A steely eyed Xabi Alonso made it abundantly clear what he thought of the performance by repeating the insistence that Chelsea “can do better” three times in a matter of seconds.

Coventry are desperately short of goals. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesFulham hardly tore Coventry apart but Frank Lampard’s hosts were typically toothless once again. The Premier League’s lowest scorers scarcely looked like adding to their meager tally with just two shots on target. The most trouble Coventry caused Fulham’s Bernd Leno was when Ephron Mason-Clark inadvertently kicked the goalkeeper in the groin.

Promising results and performances are hard to come by for Crystal Palace. / Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesCrystal Palace had denied Newcastle a single shot on target across the opening 45 minutes. Yet, they were trailing within 120 seconds of the restart.Pierre Sage’s team talk had a disastrous effect and the second half crumpling inspired boos from a restless Selhurst Park. Whether the beaten French boss will be around to deliver another address to his players is very much up in the air.

Thierno Barry had a thankless task at the Emirates. / Julian Finney/Getty ImagesThe only people who took more of a battering at the Emirates on Saturday than Everton’s players were the luckless Arsenal fans exposed to the torrential downpour in the front row.The Toffees scarcely had a sniff, with their efforts punctured by an early concession. After tumbling 1–0 down, Everton bizarrely opted to press Arsenal—perhaps Bruno Fernandes had been on the phone—which only played into the hands of their hosts.
The bench getting around Enciso. 🙌 pic.twitter.com/kljs1LHQ8U

Ipswich spent the bulk of the contest shunted firmly onto the back foot. Nottingham Forest leaped upon the hosts’ sloppy buildup play in the first half and calmly dealt with the direct game Ipswich reverted to in the second 45 minutes. Neither approach worked yet the Tractor Boys still emerged with an even share of the spoils. As Forest’s Oliver Glasner shrugged: “It is football.”

Brentford had a battle on their hands on Sunday. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesFor a Brentford side whose only defeat of the season came against Liverpool after being reduced to 10 men, Sunday’s stalemate away to newly promoted opposition inspired an understandably frustrating reaction.“We have to be better,” manager Keith Andrews and wingback Michael Kayode both stressed, with some justification.

The wind caused havoc at the Stadium of Light. / Ian MacNicol/Getty ImagesThe conditions got the better of both teams at the Stadium of Light. The storm sweeping across the U.K. undoubtedly played a major factor in the technical flaws on display, with each side combining to complete just 73% of their passes (the Premier League average is above 82%). As Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford so eloquently put it: “The wind was obviously extremely windy.”

It was all a bit messy in Sunderland. / ANDY BUCHANAN/AFP/Getty ImagesSunderland’s Premier League winless streak may have extended to six games on Sunday, but Régis Le Bris was enthused by the performance behind a goalless draw. As he pointed out after watching a contest defined by more grit than grace, “We were Sunderland today.”
Another away game, another goal ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/DT39808mi2

Enzo Maresca had been able to rely upon two certainties during his record-breaking start to the Premier League season: Erling Haaland’s goals and Gianluigi Donnarumma’s saves. His striker continued to deliver but the Italian goalkeeper let Nicolas Jackson’s daisy-cutter scuttle under his huge frame.City were caught cold by Villa’s tactical setup and deservedly trailed 1–0 after six minutes. The visitors grew into the contest, taking advantage of that questionably funded wealth of playing talent, but the ball would not fall their way for once. “It was a good game, good performance,” Maresca insisted, “but unfortunately we lost.”
Continuing our unbeaten streak at the MKM 🔥 pic.twitter.com/tIx6TR0U6z

In a bitty game which will test the creativity of highlights package editors everywhere, Hull gave as good as they got. Both sides amassed 1.8 xG and two big chances, with one spurned apiece. The Tigers boss Sergej Jakirović was not alone in hailing a draw as “a fair result.”

Fabian Hürzeler was not impressed. / Jan Kruger/Getty ImagesFabian Hürzeler drilled to the heart of Sunday’s clash at Anfield. “The difference was just that they scored and we didn’t.” Brighton went close to breaking the deadlock through Yasin Ayari before Pascal Groß inadvertently picked out the back of his own net while trying to block Florian Wirtz’s shot. Alexander Isak’s second two minutes later whisked the contest away from Brighton, who would still out-shoot and out-run their illustrious hosts on a day of frustration.“It was a missed opportunity for us,” Hürzeler huffed.
Goodnight, Fulham fam. 🤍 pic.twitter.com/foItoNI8tf
